tasks.title: a runner timeout is a real bound, even when the runner spawns children
deliverables: spawn each runner in its own process group; the timeout kills the group, not just the direct child
resolve on 'exit' plus a bounded stream drain, instead of waiting for 'close' — a grandchild holding the pipe can defer 'close' forever
a stream error retains the bytes already collected instead of discarding the transcript
acceptanceCriteria: dispatchRunner returns within a bounded margin of timeoutMs even when the runner spawns a child that inherits stdout
the transcript is still retained on that path — always retained, including on timeout and flood
no grandchild survives the timeout
a stream error never yields a null transcript when bytes were already collected
the existing timeout test uses the FORKING shape (no exec), so the regression is actually covered
verification: the grandchild case completes in about the timeout, not the child's full sleep
tasks.risk: concurrency: process-group signalling and stream teardown; a wrong grace window turns a hang into a truncated transcript

statusDetail.evidence: Three fixes in src/runner/dispatch.ts: (1) runners spawn detached so they lead their own process group, and the timeout kills the group via negative pid with a fallback to the direct child; (2) resolution awaits 'exit' not 'close', then drains stdio with a bounded 2s grace and destroys the stream if it does not finish — 'close' waits on pipes a grandchild can hold open forever; (3) collectBounded never rejects, so a stream fault retains the bytes already read instead of discarding the transcript, and the fault is reported in notes. Measured: a 500ms timeout on 'echo; sleep 30' (sh FORKS sleep) now returns in 508ms with the transcript retained and no orphan; before the fix the identical call took 30s. Regression tests use the forking shape and assert the bound, retention, and that no grandchild survives. 210 tests pass across five consecutive runs; tsc clean.

statusDetail.evidence: Authorization is free: probeAuth runs each runner's own status command — claude auth status (loggedIn), codex doctor --json (a checks entry with category=auth), cursor-agent status --format json (isAuthenticated). Only an explicit boolean counts; anything else is unknown and changes nothing, so a missing subcommand never takes a working harness out of service. A free check may demote to no or enrich the detail; only a real dispatch promotes to yes. canonicalModel() resolves aliases and decorated ids to one identity, closing a false-independence hole: 'opus' derived family 'opus' while cursor's claude-opus-5-thinking-high derived 'claude', so two names for one model passed the reviewer-independence guard (88 of cursor's 193 published models are claude-*). sonnet vs opus stays independent. cursor rows corrected: mechanical stays blank because composer-2.5 publishes no tier ladder (operator chose composer over the gpt-5.3-codex ladder to keep three distinct identities), and the 'no effort flag' comment was wrong. 232 tests pass across five consecutive runs, tsc clean; verified against the real CLIs — all three read authed=yes.
